ADU Shortlist

Companion to the Western Relocation Atlas · listings read October 7–8, 2026

ADU Shortlist

Every for-sale home between $300k and $950k that I found with a second unit already built, in the Denver, Fort Collins, Boulder, Colorado Springs, Salt Lake, Seattle and Bellingham areas (Salt Lake includes south Davis County and Eden). Listings that only said a unit “could be” added were left out. Each home is scored on its neighborhood, with the same seven criteria and colors as the atlas; drag the weights and the scores and ranks recalculate.

    How to read it

    • Evidence. “Permit on file” means a city or county permit for the second unit shows in the listing’s public permit history. “Claimed legal” means the listing says the unit is legal, permitted, approved or registered, or the county records the property as two or more units; neither is proof. “Described” means the listing states a kitchen, a bathroom and its own entrance (or the unit is a separate building). “Thin” means at least one of those is missing.
    • Score and rank. The score is the neighborhood’s, not the house’s. Rank compares it with every neighborhood in the same atlas area that passes the budget and airport filters, so a listing can outrank the area’s own best-three average.
    • Placement. Homes are placed in a neighborhood from the listing’s map position. The first Denver and Salt Lake City listings were placed from street addresses by hand and can land in the next neighborhood over when they sit near a boundary.
    • Map. The pin beside each address opens a map of that metro with the home marked; “Show all on map” shows every listing that passes the current filters. Dots are colored by neighborhood score. Two pins (5704 Santa Clara Rd, Indian Hills, and 821 S 700 E, Salt Lake City) are placed approximately.
    • Big garages. None of these homes is on the Big Garage Shortlist. That page flags five homes whose shop or outbuilding has some living space (a bunkhouse, a studio, a bath and wet bar) as “Maybe”; they did not meet the bar for this list.
    • Colorado Springs area. One capped pass on October 10, 2026 over El Paso and Teller counties (Redfin description searches for adu, in-law, carriage, accessory and kitchenette). Five of the 16 are new-construction homes from one builder northeast of the city, each with a one-bedroom unit over a detached garage; one is still being built and a seventh, not yet started, was left out. Many older west-side listings only offered "ADU potential" and were not kept.
    • Bellingham area. One small capped pass on October 10, 2026 covering Bellingham, Ferndale, Lynden and Everson, then Deming, Acme and Sudden Valley (Blaine and Sumas not searched). One pin (4290 South Pass Rd) is placed at its ZIP code. Treat it as a sample.
    • Walkable core. Replaces plain walkability. It scores access to a walkable town centre, not whether the home’s own street is walkable: full credit within about a 20-minute bike ride (5 km), fading out by about a 10–15 minute drive (15 km). A big downtown counts fully; a small main street counts less, by an amount you set with Small-core credit in Weights (60% to start). Shown as access out of 100, not a percentile. Hover a cell for the core it uses. Weighted 4 by default.
    • Schools. Test results of the public schools within 3 km (the district average where none is that close): how many grade levels above or below the U.S. average students score in grades 3–8, 2009–19, from Stanford’s Education Data Archive. Percentile among 15,188 western neighborhoods. Scores track family income closely, so read them alongside Growth.
    • Growth. How much those same students improve each year from grade 3 to 8, compared with the U.S. average rate. It reflects the schools more than who lives nearby, and it often disagrees with Schools. Percentile across Colorado, Utah and Washington.
    • Pre-K. Two numbers for children under 6. Top: Montessori, Waldorf, Reggio-inspired and nature-based programs nearby. Bottom: top-rated programs nearby (NAEYC-accredited, Colorado Shines 4–5, Washington Early Achievers 4–5). Percentiles within each state, since the states rate differently; Utah’s bottom number counts NAEYC only.
    • K–8. Public and charter Montessori, Waldorf-method, EL Education and IB Primary Years schools within about a 20-minute drive. Percentile across all three states. None of these lists has a public program in Seattle itself.
    • School weights. Hover any school number for counts and details. Growth, Pre-K and K–8 start at zero in Weights, so they change the score only if you turn them up.
    • Prices and status are as read on October 7–8, 2026, mostly from Redfin. Listings sell and prices drop, so open the link before relying on a row.
    • Before an offer, ask the seller for the permit and the certificate of occupancy for the unit, and check the city’s or county’s own permit records.

    How this was put together

    I searched Redfin for homes listed between $300k and $950k whose descriptions mention a second unit (ADU, carriage house, mother-in-law, basement apartment, guest house and similar wording), read each listing, and kept only homes where the unit already exists, not ones that merely “could be” added. The evidence level records how well the listing or public records back the unit up. Each home is placed in its 2010 census tract and given that neighborhood’s scores from the Western Relocation Atlas: seven criteria, each a percentile among 15,188 western neighborhoods, combined with the weights you set. Walkable core measures distance to the nearest walkable town centre (the atlas’s town centres where the national walkability index is at least 10 of 20), scaled by how many such neighborhoods lie within 2 km of it. Schools uses Stanford’s Education Data Archive, which puts every public school’s test results on one national scale. Growth, from the same archive, measures how much students improve from grade 3 to 8, which says more about the schools themselves and less about who lives nearby. Rank compares the neighborhood with every other one in the same metro that fits the $300k–$950k budget and has an airline airport within about 100 km. K–8 counts public and charter Montessori, Waldorf-method, EL Education and IB Primary Years schools from their own directories. Preschool access counts licensed programs from the Colorado and Washington state files, Utah directories and NAEYC’s accredited list, with nearer programs counting more. Searches were capped to keep costs down, so treat each list as a strong sample rather than a complete census, and check the listing before acting on a row.
